title: Romanian War of Independence
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Romanian War of Independence", at revision 1381161282, opens: "The Romanian War of Independence is the name used in Romanian historiography to refer to the phase of the Russo-Turkish War (1877–78), in which Romania, fighting on the Russian side of the war, gained independence from the Ottoman Empire. On 16 April [O.S. 4 April] 1877, Romania and the Russian Empire signed a treaty at Bucharest under which Russian troops were allowed to pass through Romanian territory, with the condition that Russia respected the integrity of Romania. Consequently, the mobilization of the Romanian troops also began, and around 114,000 soldiers were massed in the south of the country to defend against an eventual attack of the Ottoman forces from south of the Danube. On 24 April [O.S. 12 April] 1877, Russia declared war on the Ottoman Empire and its troops entered Romania through the newly built Eiffel Bridge, on their way to the Ottoman Empire. Due to great losses, the Russian Empire asked Romania to intervene. On 24 July [O.S. 12 July] 1877, the first Romanian Army units crossed the Danube and joined forces with the Russian Army." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q3778687, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "Independence War of Romania as part of the Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
